h2: Explore every Portable Office size & its applications
intro: Team sizes shown are layout guidance based on typical workstation plans — your drawing confirms exact capacity.

panels.paragraph: The smallest standard portable office puts a working desk, files and a visitor chair inside 100 sq ft, delivered as one factory-finished unit. It suits a single supervisor or a two-person admin point where plot space is tight, and it is the fastest size to place, power and start using. If the team is likely to grow past three people during the project, step up to the 20×8 or 20×10 — the rate per square foot drops as the floor grows. Like every size, it arrives wired, insulated and AC-provisioned, with the same 12-month workmanship warranty.

A narrow-width office that runs along a boundary wall or gate line where a 10 ft deep unit will not fit. The 160 sq ft plan takes three to four workstations in a row, with the door at the end or on the long side to suit the plot. Builders use it as the gate-side office for security, billing and visitor handling, and the slim body travels on a standard trailer with no special escort. Pick it when depth, not floor area, is your constraint. Power points run the length of the row, so each desk position is served without extension boards.

The reference SAMAN office and our most-ordered size. 200 sq ft seats four to six people as an open workstation row, or three desks plus a partitioned manager cabin on the approved drawing. Every rate on our price ladder is set from this size, which makes it the benchmark to compare any quotation against. Project managers specify it by default — fitted electricals, AC provision and insulation as standard, working from the day it lands. If you compare only one size across suppliers, compare this one — it exposes the real rate difference fastest.

panels.h3: 20×12 ft — the office with a meeting corner
panels.paragraph: Two extra feet of width over the 20×10 change how the room plans: a meeting corner, a manager bay or a records wall fits alongside five to seven workstations in 240 sq ft. This is the size where a site office stops being one row of desks and starts zoning — a front area for visitors, the working area behind. Choose it when client meetings happen at site and a 20×10 would seat them at a working desk instead of a table. The extra width costs ₹41,040 over the 20×10 — usually the cheapest meeting room a project will ever buy.

A long-plan 300 sq ft office that partitions cleanly into two rooms — typically a six-to-eight person work area plus a private manager or meeting room. The 30 ft body still moves as one unit on a standard trailer, so you get a genuine two-room site headquarters without joining modules. It is the most common pick for offices that host both daily engineering work and weekly review meetings in the same footprint. The second room doubles as a records store between reviews. Partition position is set on the drawing, so the office-to-meeting split matches how your team actually works.

The corridor-plan office: 320 sq ft arranged as a single long row of workstations, made for sites where units line up along a boundary or between structures. Seven to nine people work in line, with door positions fixed on the approved drawing before fabrication. Rail, road and pipeline projects favour it because it matches the linear space they actually have — and it ships complete on a 40 ft open trailer. Door and window positions repeat cleanly across a row of identical units. If your site has depth for a 10 ft unit, the 40×10 gives more floor at a lower rate per square foot.

A full project headquarters in one lift: 400 sq ft that plans into departments — engineering, billing, stores documentation — with space for a reception point at the door. Eight to twelve people work comfortably, and partitions are set on your drawing before the shell is fabricated. If the office roster is above eight or the project runs multi-year, start here rather than joining two smaller units later. Reception, records and meeting zones are marked on the drawing you approve. It is the largest size that still plans as one open decision — beyond it, choices multiply with the rooms.

panels.h3: 20×20 ft — the square open-plan office floor
panels.paragraph: The same 400 sq ft as the 40×10 on a square plan — an open-floor office suited to team seating around clusters rather than rows. The square shape shortens supervision lines and keeps a central circulation space, which open-plan teams consistently prefer. Confirm site access for the 20 ft wide load early in planning; after that you get a floor plan no corridor-shaped unit can match. Cluster seating works without a single corridor desk, and the floor centre stays open for briefing space. Rate and price match the 40×10 exactly, so the choice is purely about the shape your plot and team need.

Our largest standard portable office: 480 sq ft that partitions into multiple rooms — cabins, a meeting room, stores and a pantry space — delivered complete as one unit. Ten to fourteen people can run a full site administration from it. At ₹1,242 per square foot it also carries the lowest rate on the ladder, so the biggest floor is the best value per foot. Beyond this size, offices become joined multi-unit layouts, quoted to drawing. Typical fit-outs pair it with a reception counter and server point, both positioned on the approved drawing.
